title: Ops Clipboard: split-and-run playbook snippets for safe, idempotent support automation
creator: Emily Chen
description:
Problem:
On-call responders and tier-1 support need a fast, auditable way to reuse vetted remediation steps without running full monolithic runbooks. Existing runbooks are long prose and frequently non-idempotent, making automation fragile. We also lack a lightweight mechanism to capture partial state snapshots and correlate telemetry for snippet runs.

Proposal:
Build 'Ops Clipboard' — a small service + UI that stores curated, parameterized, idempotent playlet snippets (YAML + run constraints). Each playlet is a first-class task that can be invoked directly, composed into ephemeral sequences, or published into canonical runbooks. Playlets will include metadata: required inputs, safety checks, reversal steps, telemetry keys for correlation, and estimated cost. The service will expose a runbooks-as-tasks API for both interactive operator flows and automated remediation pipelines.

Key design goals:
- Idempotency: every playlet must declare an idempotency key and optional pre-check/post-check hooks.
- Safety: permission gates and optional dry-run mode; execution limited by scope and rate.
- Observability: structured telemetry and correlator IDs that tie playlet execution to traces, logs, and cost metrics.
- Composability: allow safe inline composition of playlets; enforce explicit dataflow and no implicit shared-state.
- Auditability: immutable execution records, links to PRs and author, and changelog for each playlet.

Non-goals:
- This is not a full runbook translator/compiler; rather it is a curated snippet catalog for operators and automation.
acceptance_criteria: Service: Ops Clipboard endpoint implements POST /playlets (create), GET /playlets/{id}, POST /playlets/{id}/run and supports dry-run and live-run modes.
Playlet schema: playlet manifest schema validated against JSON/YAML schema including inputs, outputs, idempotency_key and safety_policy.
Safety and RBAC: only users or automation roles in the Ops Remediation group can run production-affecting playlets; dry-run allowed to lower tiers.
Telemetry: each run emits a correlator_id that appears in tracing, logs, and the Console per-route dashboard; console shows run duration, token usage, and outcome.
Composability: show a minimal client-side composer in Console to sequence up to 5 playlets with explicit input mapping and preview dry-run results.
Audit trail: every run writes an immutable record with playlet version, inputs, outputs (truncated where sensitive), actor, and link to GitHub PR if created by CI.
E2E tests: integration tests exercising dry-run, live-run, failure/retry, and concurrent runs demonstrating idempotency guarantees (re-run returns no-op where expected).
Migration: provide a small importer that converts 10 canonical runbook steps into playlets as a demo dataset for internal ops.
